plan.contextChunk: This figure is a labeled anatomy diagram of a horizontal ellipse, drawn as a blue outline centered at the origin of a coordinate system whose horizontal axis is marked x at the right and whose vertical axis is marked y at the top, both ending in arrowheads. A red dashed segment lies along the horizontal axis and spans the full width of the curve; the words "Major Axis" sit below its left half, and its two endpoints, where the outline meets the horizontal axis, are marked with dots and labeled "Vertex" at each end. A second red dashed segment lies along the vertical axis and spans the height of the curve, labeled "Minor Axis" beside its upper half, with black dots at its ends labeled "Co-vertex" above and "Co-vertex" below. The black dot where the two dashed segments cross is labeled "Center." Two small green dots sit on the horizontal dashed segment, one on either side of the center and well inside the vertices, each labeled "Focus." Collecting every named part on a single outline lets the reader tie each term to a definite position relative to the center. The diagram supplies the vocabulary needed to set up and read the standard equation of an ellipse.

interactionPlan.concept: Every ellipse is organized around its center by four named parts — vertices, co-vertices, and foci — whose positions are fixed by the semi-major axis a, the semi-minor axis b, and the focal distance c, related by c² = a² − b².
elements: Horizontal x-axis with arrowheads at both ends, label 'x' at right end
Vertical y-axis with arrowheads at both ends, label 'y' at top
Blue ellipse outline centered at the origin, wider than tall (horizontal major axis)
Red dashed horizontal segment from left vertex to right vertex lying on the x-axis (major axis)
Red dashed vertical segment from bottom co-vertex to top co-vertex lying on the y-axis (minor axis)
Black dot at origin labeled 'Center'
Black dots at (±a, 0) where the ellipse meets the x-axis, each labeled 'Vertex'
Black dots at (0, ±b) where the ellipse meets the y-axis, each labeled 'Co-vertex' (top) and 'Co-vertex' (bottom)
Two small green dots on the major axis at (±c, 0), inside the vertices, each labeled 'Focus'
Text label 'Major Axis' below the left half of the horizontal dashed segment
Text label 'Minor Axis' to the right of the upper half of the vertical dashed segment
Alternate (toggled) parameter labels: brace/arrow marking 'a' from center to right vertex, 'b' from center to top co-vertex, 'c' from center to right focus
Alternate (toggled) readout of the standard equation x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 with live numeric values of a, b, c and the relation c² = a² − b²
Optional draggable point P on the ellipse with two straight segments P→left focus and P→right focus, annotated with their lengths and their sum

interactions.teaches: a is the distance from the center to a vertex: increasing it stretches the ellipse horizontally, pushing the vertices outward while the center and co-vertices stay put, and dragging the foci farther apart.
interactions.label: Semi-major axis a

interactions.teaches: b is the distance from the center to a co-vertex: it controls only the height, moving the co-vertices while the vertices stay fixed — and as b approaches a the foci slide toward the center.
interactions.label: Semi-minor axis b

interactions.teaches: Each named anatomical part corresponds to a number in the standard equation: vertex ↔ a, co-vertex ↔ b, focus ↔ c, with c² = a² − b².
interactions.label: Label mode

interactions.teaches: Why the foci are special: no matter where the point sits on the curve, the sum of its distances to the two foci stays equal to 2a.

demo_steps.title: The named parts
demo_steps.narration: A horizontal ellipse with its center at the origin. The red dashed major axis runs between the two vertices; the red dashed minor axis runs between the two co-vertices; two green foci sit on the major axis inside the vertices.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the major axis
demo_steps.narration: Increase a and only the width changes: the vertices slide outward, the co-vertices never move, and the foci spread farther apart as the ellipse grows more elongated.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the minor axis
demo_steps.narration: Now hold a and raise b: the co-vertices rise, the vertices stay anchored, and the foci creep toward the center because c = √(a² − b²) shrinks.

demo_steps.title: When a = b the ellipse is a circle
demo_steps.narration: Set b equal to a and c becomes zero — both foci collapse onto the center, the axes become equal, and the ellipse is just a circle of radius a.

demo_steps.title: From parts to equation
demo_steps.narration: Switch to parameter labels: the center-to-vertex distance is a, the center-to-co-vertex distance is b, and the center-to-focus distance is c, feeding directly into x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 with c² = a² − b².

demo_steps.title: The focal definition
demo_steps.narration: Drag the point around the curve and watch the two focal distances trade off — their sum is always 2a, the full length of the major axis.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The ellipse's anatomy is just three distances measured from the center — a to a vertex, b to a co-vertex, c to a focus — locked together by c² = a² − b², so changing the shape moves the foci automatically.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Centered Cartesian axes drawn thin and black with arrowheads at all four ends, 'x' labeled at the right tip and italic 'y' at the top tip. A single blue (medium-thick, steel-blue) ellipse outline centered on the origin, noticeably wider than tall in the default view. Red dashed straight segments lie exactly on the axes, spanning vertex-to-vertex horizontally and co-vertex-to-co-vertex vertically. Black filled dots mark center, both vertices, and both co-vertices; two smaller bright-green dots mark the foci on the horizontal dashed line, roughly two-thirds of the way out toward the vertices in the default state. Serif text labels: 'Vertex' outside each end of the major axis, 'Co-vertex' above the top dot and below the bottom dot, 'Focus' above each green dot, 'Center' just below-right of the origin dot, 'Major Axis' under the left half of the horizontal segment, 'Minor Axis' to the right of the upper vertical segment. In 'Equation parameters' mode the word labels are replaced by dimension arrows from the center to the right vertex ('a'), center to top co-vertex ('b'), and center to right focus ('c'), plus a small corner panel showing x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 and c² = a² − b² with live numeric values. The draggable point is an orange dot on the curve with two thin gray lines to the green foci and a readout r₁ + r₂ = 2a. Keep the viewport fixed so the learner perceives the ellipse growing and shrinking rather than the axes rescaling.

authoredContext:
Every ellipse has two axes of symmetry. The longer axis is called the major axis, and the shorter axis is called the minor axis. Each endpoint of the major axis is the vertex of the ellipse (plural: vertices), and each endpoint of the minor axis is a co-vertex of the ellipse. The center of an ellipse is the midpoint of both the major and minor axes. The axes are perpendicular at the center. The foci always lie on the major axis, and the sum of the distances from the foci to any point on the ellipse (the constant sum) is greater than the distance between the foci. See the figure.

A horizontal ellipse centered at (0, 0) in the x y coordinate system, with Major and Minor Axes, Vertices and Co-Vertices, Foci, and Center labeled.

In this section, we restrict ellipses to those that are positioned vertically or horizontally in the coordinate plane. That is, the axes will either lie on or be parallel to the x- and y-axes. Later in the chapter, we will see ellipses that are rotated in the coordinate plane.

discrepancies: Composition/scale: in the source the ellipse nearly fills the frame with the y-axis barely extending past the co-vertices, whereas the generated figure draws the vertical axis the full height of a tall canvas, leaving large empty regions above and below the ellipse and making the drawing look small and vertically stretched.

The 'Vertex' labels sit directly on the x-axis line (the axis stroke runs through the baseline area) rather than being offset above it as in the source.
The red dashed axis segments render with a tighter/darker dash than the source's clearly-spaced bright red dashes, and the ellipse stroke is thinner relative to the frame than in the source.
evaluation.notes: Faithful reproduction of the labelled-ellipse anatomy with correct primitives, colors and all source labels, plus a rich and pedagogically apt set of interactions (a/b sliders, parameter-label toggle, focal-sum drag point, 6-step tour); main weaknesses are loose vertical composition (over-long y-axis and surrounding whitespace shrinking the ellipse) and a couple of labels touching the dots/axis lines.

Increase the gap between the co-vertex dots and their labels (and nudge 'Vertex' labels further above the x-axis) so no text touches the dots or the axis strokes.
Make the red dashed major/minor axis strokes brighter with a longer dash gap and slightly thicken the blue ellipse stroke to match the source's line weights.

demo_steps.title: The named parts
demo_steps.narration: A horizontal ellipse with its center at the origin. The red dashed major axis runs between the two vertices; the red dashed minor axis runs between the two co-vertices; two green foci sit on the major axis inside the vertices.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the major axis
demo_steps.narration: Increase a and only the width changes: the vertices slide outward, the co-vertices never move, and the foci spread farther apart as the ellipse grows more elongated.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the minor axis
demo_steps.narration: Now hold a and raise b: the co-vertices rise, the vertices stay anchored, and the foci creep toward the center because c = √(a² − b²) shrinks.

demo_steps.title: When a = b the ellipse is a circle
demo_steps.narration: Set b equal to a and c becomes zero — both foci collapse onto the center, the axes become equal, and the ellipse is just a circle of radius a.

demo_steps.title: From parts to equation
demo_steps.narration: Switch to parameter labels: the center-to-vertex distance is a, the center-to-co-vertex distance is b, and the center-to-focus distance is c, feeding directly into x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 with c² = a² − b².

demo_steps.title: The focal definition
demo_steps.narration: Drag the point around the curve and watch the two focal distances trade off — their sum is always 2a, the full length of the major axis.

plan.keyInsight: The ellipse's anatomy is just three distances measured from the center — a to a vertex, b to a co-vertex, c to a focus — locked together by c² = a² − b², so changing the shape moves the foci automatically.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Centered Cartesian axes drawn thin and black with arrowheads at all four ends, 'x' labeled at the right tip and italic 'y' at the top tip. A single blue (medium-thick, steel-blue) ellipse outline centered on the origin, noticeably wider than tall in the default view. Red dashed straight segments lie exactly on the axes, spanning vertex-to-vertex horizontally and co-vertex-to-co-vertex vertically. Black filled dots mark center, both vertices, and both co-vertices; two smaller bright-green dots mark the foci on the horizontal dashed line, roughly two-thirds of the way out toward the vertices in the default state. Serif text labels: 'Vertex' outside each end of the major axis, 'Co-vertex' above the top dot and below the bottom dot, 'Focus' above each green dot, 'Center' just below-right of the origin dot, 'Major Axis' under the left half of the horizontal segment, 'Minor Axis' to the right of the upper vertical segment. In 'Equation parameters' mode the word labels are replaced by dimension arrows from the center to the right vertex ('a'), center to top co-vertex ('b'), and center to right focus ('c'), plus a small corner panel showing x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 and c² = a² − b² with live numeric values. The draggable point is an orange dot on the curve with two thin gray lines to the green foci and a readout r₁ + r₂ = 2a. Keep the viewport fixed so the learner perceives the ellipse growing and shrinking rather than the axes rescaling.

discrepancies: The red dashed major/minor axes render as a dark, low-contrast red with very tight dashes; in the source they are a vivid pure red with clearly separated dashes overlaying the black axes, so the dashed emphasis reads less strongly at a glance.

The italic 'x' axis label is placed inside the frame just below the right arrow, so it sits on top of/near the ellipse curve and the right 'Vertex' arrow, whereas in the source it sits clearly outside and to the right of the arrow tip.
The italic 'y' label is tucked immediately left of the upper arrow and crowds the 'Co-vertex' text; in the source 'y' sits above the arrow tip with clear separation from the 'Co-vertex' label.

Vertical proportions differ slightly: the generated axis/ellipse block is shifted upward in the canvas leaving a large empty band at the bottom, while the source is vertically centered and the ellipse fills more of the frame.
evaluation.notes: A very faithful reproduction of the labeled-ellipse anatomy figure with correct primitives, dots, foci and all source annotations, backed by genuinely useful a/b sliders, a parameter-label toggle, a draggable focal-sum point and a 6-step guided tour; only minor placement crowding of the x/y axis letters and a slightly muted red dashed styling hold it back.
action_items: Move the 'x' label outside the right arrow tip (and 'y' above the top arrow tip) as in the source, so neither collides with the ellipse curve, the vertex arrow, or the 'Co-vertex' text.
Brighten the dashed axes to the source's pure red and lengthen the dash pattern so the dashed major/minor axes read unmistakably as dashed at inline size.
Re-center the figure vertically (or shrink the reserved bottom space) so the ellipse occupies the canvas as tightly as it does in the source image.
Nudge the top/bottom 'Co-vertex' labels to match the source offsets (top label right of the dot at dot level, bottom label below the arrow) to avoid crowding the y-axis arrow.
